prediction.likelyOutcome: Given conceded liability, an unopposed-on-valuation trial record, and strong parcel-specific severance facts, plaintiffs are highly likely to recover a substantial just compensation award -- realistically in the high-teens-to-high-$30 millions range -- with the ultimate figure discounted from the full $44,744,774 ask to account for legitimate cap-rate and comparable-sales critiques, plus pre-judgment interest from October 2019 that is not separately quantifiable here.

issues.label: Government's Nominal/No-Compensation Theory (Pre-Existing Burden & Narrow Scope)
Appraisal Methodology Reliability Challenge (Cap Rate & Comparables)

outcome.description: After the valuation trial the Court of Federal Claims adopted Dr. Kilpatrick's before-and-after values for all thirteen parcels but struck his privacy-wall component, awarding just compensation of $42,641,740 (before values $66,179,431, after values $23,537,691) plus interest at the Moody's Aaa corporate bond rate compounded annually, against a demand of $44,744,774; it also denied the government's motion to reopen the record. No attorneys' fees were addressed in this opinion. This is the trial-level decision; no appellate ruling is reflected.

source.caseName: Kotis Associates, LLC, et al. v. United States

Record citations (Tr., JX, PX, DX) were dropped from most sentences, and within the parcel descriptions a few intervening sentences (purchase history, parking/building inventories) were omitted between retained sentences.
